items.name: G-extensions, their counts and group signatures
items.statement: For a permutation group G (a group with a faithful action on a set B_G), a G-extension of k is an extension L/k in Q̄ with a permutation-group isomorphism Gal(L/k) ≃ G, the Galois closure group acting on the embeddings L → L̃ over k (Definition 6.7); isomorphisms of permutation groups are pairs (φ, π) compatible with the actions, and Aut_perm(G) = N_{Sym B_G}(G). E_k(G, X) is the set of G-extensions with absolute discriminant Disc(L) ≤ X, N_k(G, X) the number with Disc(L/k) = Nm(disc(L/k)) ≤ X, E_k(m, X) the degree-2^m 2-extensions. The group signature of K/k is the tuple (Σ_v) over real places v of k of the conjugacy classes of complex conjugation, and E^Σ_k(G, X) those of signature Σ.
items.locator: §1.5, p.6; §6, pp.29–30; Definition 6.7, p.33, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Relative class groups and ℓ-torsion
items.statement: For L/K, Cl_{L/K} = ker(Nm_{L/K} : Cl_L → Cl_K), h(L/K) = |Cl_{L/K}|, h_ℓ(L/K) = |Cl_{L/K}[ℓ]|. If (ℓ, [L : K]) = 1 then Nm_{L/K} ∘ ι is multiplication by [L : K] on Cl_K[ℓ], so Cl_L[ℓ] ≃ Cl_{L/K}[ℓ] × Cl_K[ℓ] and h_ℓ(L) = h_ℓ(K)h_ℓ(L/K).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: The Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet conjecture (1.1)
items.statement: For a number field k, a transitive permutation group G and a prime p ∤ |G|, conjecturally there is c_{k,G,p} > 0 with lim_{X→∞}|E_k(G, X)|^{−1}Σ_{K∈E_k(G,X)}|Cl_K[p]| = c_{k,G,p}. More precisely, Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet fix the enriched signature (the Galois-module structure of O_L^* ⊗ ℚ, equivalently ⊕_v Ind^Γ_{Γ_v}ℚ) and predict averages of functions of the class group avoiding bad Sylow subgroups; (1.1) needs in addition that the frequencies of enriched signatures exist.
items.note: A conjecture; proven before this paper only for (G, p) = (S₂, 3) (Davenport–Heilbronn, Datskovsky–Wright) and (S₃, 2) (Bhargava). Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Class number of a number field
items.statement: The class number h(K) is the cardinality of the (finite) ideal class group of O_K.
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/ClassNumber.lean:64 at 082e2d3.

items.name: Regulator of a number field
items.statement: Rg_K is the covolume of the logarithmic embedding of the unit group O_K^* modulo torsion.
items.locator: §1.5, p.6; Lemma 2.4 and the proof of Lemma 2.1, pp.8–9, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Units/Regulator.lean:266 at 082e2d3.

items.name: Dirichlet's unit theorem
items.statement: Every unit of O_K is uniquely a root of unity times a product of powers of a fundamental system of r₁ + r₂ − 1 units.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.1, pp.8–9, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Units/DirichletTheorem.lean:506 at 082e2d3.

items.name: Ellenberg–Venkatesh: small elements lie in subfields, and the torsion lemma ([EV07, Lemmas 2.2–2.3])
items.statement: An element of a number field whose height is smaller than a fixed power of the discriminant of the field it generates lies in a proper subfield ([EV07, Lemma 2.2]). If there are M primes of L of norm < Disc(L)^θ, 0 < θ < 1/(4ℓ([L:ℚ] − 1)), none extended from a proper subfield, then |Cl_L[ℓ]| ≪_{[L:ℚ],θ,ε} Disc(L)^{1/2+ε}/M (2.2).
items.locator: §2, (2.2), p.7; proof of Lemma 2.1, p.9, citing [EV07], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: Imported; used in its relative form. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 2.1 (relative Ellenberg–Venkatesh)
items.statement: Let L/K be an extension with d := [L : K], ℓ ≥ 1 and 0 < θ < 1/(4ℓ(d − 1)). Suppose there are M pairs of distinct primes (℘_i, ℘̄_i) of L and integers a_i, b_i with (1) ℘_i ∩ O_K = ℘̄_i ∩ O_K and Nm_{L/K}(℘_i)^{a_i} = Nm_{L/K}(℘̄_i)^{b_i}; (2) Nm(℘_i)^{a_i} = Nm(℘̄_i)^{b_i} < Disc(L/K)^θ; (3) no intermediate field K ⊆ H ⊊ L from a prime of which powers of both ℘_i and ℘̄_i are extended. Then |Cl_{L/K}[ℓ]| = O_{[L:ℚ],θ,ε}(Disc(L/K)^{1/2+ε}Disc(K)^{(d−1)/2+ε}/M) (2.1). For primes split completely in L/K, (1) and (3) are automatic and (2) reads Nm(℘_i ∩ O_K) < Disc(L/K)^θ.
items.locator: Lemma 2.1, Remark 2.2, p.7; proof pp.8–10, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19 (misprints E2, E3; gap E1)
items.note: Statement with d = [L : K] as in the proof and the applications (E2). Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Lemmas 2.3–2.4 (cokernel of the norm and the trivial bound)
items.statement: coker(Nm_{L/K} : Cl_L → Cl_K) ≃ Gal(M/K) with M = H_K ∩ L (H_K the Hilbert class field of K), so it has order ≤ [L : K]. Hence, with d = [L : K], (Rg(L)/Rg(K))h(L/K) ≪_{[L:ℚ],ε} Disc(L/K)^{1/2+ε}Disc(K)^{(d−1)/2+ε} and h_ℓ(L/K) ≪_{[L:ℚ],ε} Disc(L/K)^{1/2+ε}Disc(K)^{(d−1)/2+ε}, using Brauer–Siegel and Rg(L)/Rg(K) ≫_{[L:ℚ]} 1 (Friedman–Skoruppa).
items.locator: Lemmas 2.3–2.4 and proofs, pp.7–8, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 3.1 and Corollary 3.2 (uniform bounds for S₃ cubics and h₃ of quadratic extensions)
items.statement: For a number field F with h = h₂(F), D_F = Disc(F) and X ≥ 1, Σ_{[K:F]=2, Disc(K/F)≤X}h₃(K/F) ≪_{[F:ℚ],ε} D_F^ε · (hX^{3/2}D_F^{1/2} if X ≤ D_Fh^{−2/3}; h^{1/3}X^{1/2}D_F^{3/2} if D_Fh^{−2/3} ≤ X ≤ D_F²h^{2/3}; XD_F^{1/2} if D_F²h^{2/3} ≤ X ≤ D_F^{5/2}h^{2/3}; h^{2/3}D_F³ if D_F^{5/2}h^{2/3} ≤ X ≤ D_F³h^{2/3}; X if X ≥ D_F³h^{2/3}), and the same bound holds for N_F(S₃, X). Hence both are O_{[F:ℚ],ε}(Disc(F)^{1+ε}h₂(F)^{2/3}X) (Corollary 3.2), i.e. O(Disc(F)^{4/3+ε}X) in general. The implied constant is ineffective through Brauer–Siegel (Remark 3.3).
items.locator: Theorem 3.1, Corollary 3.2, Remark 3.3, p.10; proof §3.4, p.19, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: The five ranges were checked to join continuously. The first explicit base-field dependence of a count of non-abelian (S₃) extensions (§1.3). Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 3.4 and Lemma 3.5 (small range: class field theory)
items.statement: The number of extensions L/F in Q̄ with Disc(L/F) = n and [L : F] ≤ 3 is O_{[F:ℚ],ε}(n^{1/2+ε}h₂(F)Disc(F)^{1/2+ε}); hence N_F(S₃, X) + N_F(C₃, X) + N_F(S₂, X) = O_{[F:ℚ],ε}(X^{3/2+ε}Disc(F)^{1/2+ε}h₂(F)). Proof: quadratic K/F correspond to characters of the idèle class group, determined up to Hom(Cl_F, C₂) by their local restrictions; S₃ cubics with resolvent K are cyclic cubic extensions of K counted by h₃(K/F) (Lemma 2.4).
items.locator: Proposition 3.4, Lemma 3.5 and proof, p.11, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19 (error E4 in the proof)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 3.6 (large range: counting cubic rings)
items.statement: For X ≥ Disc(F)³h₂(F)^{2/3}, the number N_{O_F,3}(X) of isomorphism classes of cubic rings over O_F with 0 < Disc(R/O_F) ≤ X satisfies N_{O_F,3}(X) ≪_{[F:ℚ],ε} Disc(F)^εX. In general N_{O_F,α}(X) ≪ X·Res_{s=1}ζ_F(s) + X^{−1/2−ε}h₂(F)Disc(F)^{9/2+ε} (3.3), by smoothed Perron, contour shift to ℜ(s) = −1/2 − ε past the poles at 1 and 5/6 (no pole at 0 by Lemma 3.8), the functional equation and Lemma 3.10, and Landau's bound Res_{s=1}ζ_F ≪ Disc(F)^ε.
items.locator: Proposition 3.6 and proof, pp.12, 15, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 3.7 (Shintani zeta functions over a number field)
items.statement: For each signature α, ξ_{F,α}(s) = Σ_{R: sgn R = α}|Aut_{O_F}(R)|^{−1}Disc(R/O_F)^{−s} over cubic rings converges for ℜ(s) > 1; it continues meromorphically with simple poles only at s = 1 and 5/6, with residues 𝔄_F(1 + 3^{−r(α)−r₂(F)}) and 𝔅_F·3^{−r(α)/2} (r(α) = #{v : α_v ≃ ℝ³}); it satisfies ξ_{F,α}(1 − s) = (3^{6s−2}π^{−4s}Γ(s)²Γ(s − 1/6)Γ(s + 1/6))^{[F:ℚ]}Disc(F)^{4s−2}Σ_β c_{αβ}(s)ξ̂_{F,β}(s) with the dual series ξ̂ (restricted local conditions at v | 3), 0 < ξ̂_{F,α}(s) < ξ_{F,α}(s) for real s > 1; and (s − 1)(s − 5/6)ξ, (s − 1)(s − 5/6)ξ̂ are entire of order 1.
items.locator: Proposition 3.7 and proof, pp.12–13, citing Shintani [Shi72], Wright [Wri82, Wri85], Datskovsky–Wright [DW86], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: AN.8 plans Sato–Shintani prehomogeneous-vector-space zeta functions with their functional equations.

items.name: Lemmas 3.8–3.11 (vanishing at 0, orders, uniform and convexity bounds for Shintani zeta)
items.statement: If [F : ℚ] ≥ 2 then ξ_{F,α}(0) = 0, since each c_{αβ}(s) vanishes to order [F : ℚ] at s = 1 (Lemma 3.8). For a cubic étale algebra A/F, the orders O ⊂ A with [O_A : O]² = n have Dirichlet series f_A(s) = ζ_F(4s)ζ_F(6s − 1)ζ_A(2s)/ζ_A(4s) (Datskovsky–Wright, Lemma 3.9). For σ > 3/2, ξ_{F,α}(σ + it) ≪_{[F:ℚ],σ,ε} Disc(F)^{1/2+ε}h₂(F) (Lemma 3.10), and for −1/2 ≤ σ ≤ 3/2, ξ_{F,α}(σ + it) = O(h₂(F)Disc(F)^{7/2−2σ+ε}(1 + |t|)^{2[F:ℚ](3/2−σ)+ε}) by Phragmén–Lindelöf (Lemma 3.11).
items.locator: Lemmas 3.8–3.11 and proofs, pp.13–15, citing [DW86, Theorem 6.1], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: The Phragmén–Lindelöf interpolation between the bounds at σ = 3/2 and σ = −1/2 was checked. Routed to AnalyticNumberTheory AN.3/AN.4/AN.8 as a source.

items.name: Propositions 3.12, 3.15 and Lemmas 3.13–3.14 (intermediate range: propagation of orders)
items.statement: Σ_{[K:F]=2, Disc(K/F)≤X}h₃(K/F) and N_F(S₃, X) are both ≪_{[F:ℚ],ε} Disc(F)^{1/2+ε}κ_F^{−2}X^{1/2}(Disc(F)h₂(F)^{1/3} + X^{1/2}) with κ_F = Res_{s=1}ζ_F. Lemma 3.13: the orders in F × K and in the non-Galois cubics with resolvent K and disc(L/F) = disc(K/F) have generating series (h₃(K/F)/2)Disc(K/F)^{−s}ζ_F(2s)ζ_F(6s − 1)Σ_{𝔞 ⊆ O_K sq. free, [𝔞] ∈ 3Cl_K + Cl_F}Nm(𝔞)^{−2s}. Lemma 3.14: for X ≥ C Disc(F)^{1/2+δ}κ_F^{−1}, #{𝔞 ⊆ O_F : Nm 𝔞 ≤ X} ≫ κ_FX. Each K therefore contributes ≫ h₃(K/F)Y^{1/2}κ_F/Disc(K/F)^{1/2} orders to N_{O_F,3}(Y), which Proposition 3.6 bounds; S₃ cubics then follow by [DW88, Lemma 6.2].
items.locator: Propositions 3.12, 3.15, Lemmas 3.13–3.14 and proofs, pp.15–19, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19 (misprint E5 in Lemma 3.14)
items.note: The Dirichlet-series identity of Lemma 3.13 was re-derived from Lemma 3.9. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 4.1 (standard properties of ray class L-functions)
items.statement: For a nontrivial ray class character χ of k with q_χ = Nm(𝔣_χ)Disc(k): the number of zeros ρ with |ℑρ − t| ≤ 1 is O_{[k:ℚ]}(log((t + 1)q_χ)); and for −3/2 ≤ ℜ(s) ≤ 2, −L′/L(s, χ) = −(r₁⁺(χ) + r₂)/s − (r₁⁻(χ) + r₂)/(s + 1) − Σ_{|s−ρ|<1}(s − ρ)^{−1} + O_{[k:ℚ]}(log((|s| + 1)q_χ)), via the completed L-function and its functional equation.
items.locator: §4, Lemma 4.1, pp.19–20, citing [IK04, Proposition 5.7], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: AN.4 plans Hecke L-functions with completed functional equations; AN.3 plans zero counting.

items.name: Theorem 4.2 (log-free zero density for ray class L-functions)
items.statement: There is c = c([k : ℚ]) > 0 such that for Q, T > 1, 1/2 ≤ σ < 1 and ε > 0, Σ_{Nm 𝔮≤Q}Σ*_{χ mod 𝔮}N_χ(σ, T) ≪_{[k:ℚ],ε} (Disc(k)QT)^{c(1−σ)+ε}, the inner sum over primitive ray class characters of conductor 𝔮 and N_χ(σ, T) counting zeros with ℜρ ∈ (σ, 1), |ℑρ| ≤ T.
items.locator: Theorem 4.2, p.20, citing Lemke Oliver–Thorner [Pas17, Proposition A.2] and Thorner–Zaman [TZ21, Theorem 1.2], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: Imported. Routed to AnalyticNumberTheory AN.3/AN.4/AN.8 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 4.3 (most quadratic extensions have many small split primes)
items.statement: For ε₁ > 0 and X ≥ 2 there is E = E(k, X, ε₁) ⊂ {F/k quadratic, Disc(F/k) ≤ X} with |E| ≪_{[k:ℚ],ε₁} Disc(k)^{ε₁}X^{ε₁}, such that for F ∉ E and 4 ≤ Y ≤ X, π_k(Y; F, e) ≥ (1/8)π_k(Y/2) − C_{[k:ℚ],ε₁}Y^{σ₁}log²(X Disc(k)) with σ₁ = max(1 − ε₁/(4c), 1/2). E consists of the F whose character χ_{F/k} has a zero with ℜρ > σ₁, |ℑρ| ≤ X^{1/2}; the proof is the explicit formula with Lemma 4.1.
items.locator: Lemma 4.3 and proof, pp.20–22, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: Routed to AnalyticNumberTheory AN.3/AN.4/AN.8 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 4.4 (Zaman's effective lower bound for prime ideals)
items.statement: There are absolute effective γ, β, D₀ > 0 such that if Disc(k) ≥ D₀ and Y ≥ Disc(k)^β then π_k(Y) ≫_{[k:ℚ]} Disc(k)^{−γ}Y/log Y (Zaman: β = 35, γ = 19; also β = 694, γ = 5 [TZ17]; γ = 1/[k : ℚ] with inexplicit β [TZ19a]).
items.locator: Lemma 4.4, p.22, citing [Zam17], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: Imported. Routed to AnalyticNumberTheory AN.3/AN.4/AN.8 as a source.

items.name: Brauer–Siegel, Landau and Friedman–Skoruppa inputs
items.statement: Res_{s=1}ζ_F(s) ≪_{[F:ℚ],ε} Disc(F)^ε (Landau) and ≫_{[F:ℚ],ε} Disc(F)^{−ε} (Brauer–Siegel/Siegel, ineffective unless ζ_F has no Landau–Siegel zero; Stark), h(F)Rg(F) ≍ Disc(F)^{1/2+o(1)} in bounded degree, and Rg(L)/Rg(K) ≫_{[L:ℚ]} 1 for L ⊇ K (Friedman–Skoruppa).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.4, p.8; §3.2, p.15; §3.4, p.19, citing [Bra47], [Sta74], [FS99], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: Routed to AnalyticNumberTheory AN.3/AN.4/AN.8 as a source.

items.name: Klüners–Wang inputs: towers and 2-torsion ([KW20, Lemma 2.3, Theorem 2.7])
items.statement: If G ⊂ S_{ℓ^r} is an ℓ-group and Gal(E/F) ≃ G, there is a tower F = F₀ ⊂ F₁ ⊂ … ⊂ F_r = E with Gal(F_{i+1}/F_i) = C_ℓ (Lemma 5.4). For a 2-extension F/k, h₂(F) ≪_{[F:ℚ],ε} Disc(F)^εh₂(k)^{[F:k]} (Lemma 5.6).
items.locator: Lemmas 5.4, 5.6, pp.23, citing Klüners–Wang [KW20], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: Imported. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 5.8 (number of quadratic extensions)
items.statement: N_k(C₂, X) = O_{[k:ℚ],ε}(h₂(k)Disc(k)^εX), by class field theory and a Perron-formula count of ideals of bounded norm using the convexity bound and Landau.
items.locator: Lemma 5.8 and proof, p.25, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 5.1 (uniform tail estimate) and Corollary 5.5
items.statement: For each m ≥ 2 there are δ_m > 0 and α_m, depending on m and [k : ℚ], such that for all X, Y > 0, Σ_{F_m/F_{m−1}/…/F₁/k: Disc(F_{m−1})≥Y, X/2≤Disc(F_m)≤X}h₃(F_m/k) = O_{ε,[k:ℚ],m}((X/Y^{1−ε} + X^{1−δ_m})Disc(k)^{α_m}), summing over towers of relative quadratic extensions. With Y = 1: the sum over X/2 ≤ Disc(F_m) ≤ X is O(X Disc(k)^{α_m}) (Corollary 5.5). Proof: for m = 2, split Disc(F₁) into the noncritical range (Lemma 5.7, via Theorem 3.1 and Lemma 5.6) and the critical range [X^{1/3−δ₀}, X^{1/3+δ₀}] (Lemma 5.9: Lemma 2.1 with θ = 1/20 and small split primes from Lemmas 4.3–4.4 outside exceptional sets); then induct on m.
items.locator: Theorem 5.1, Remarks 5.2–5.3, Corollary 5.5, Lemmas 5.7, 5.9 and proofs, §5, pp.22–29, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19 (misprint E5)
items.note: The exponent bookkeeping of Lemmas 5.7 and 5.9 (for example X^{1−δ₁/3+δ₀(3/2−2δ₁)} < X^{0.998}) and of the induction was checked. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 6.2 (counting 2-extensions)
items.statement: |E_k(m, X)| ∼ D_mX with D_m = Σ_{F∈E_k(m−1,∞)}Res_{s=1}ζ_F/(2^{r₂(F)}ζ_F(2)Disc(F)²). For a transitive 2-group G = C₂ ≀ H with a transposition and a group signature Σ, |E^Σ_k(G, X)| ∼ D_{G,Σ}X and |E_k(G, X)| ∼ D_GX with D_G = Σ_{F∈E_k(H,∞)}2^{2^{m−1}−r₂(F)}Res ζ_F/(ζ_F(2)Disc(F)²) > 0, and D_{G,Σ} > 0 if some H-extension has signature Σ̄. If G has no transposition, |E_k(G, X)| = O_{k,G,ε}(X^{1/2+ε}).
items.locator: Theorem 6.2 and proof, pp.30–31, citing Malle [Mal02, Mal04], Klüners–Malle [KM04, Corollary 7.3], Klüners [Klü12, Lemma 5.5, Theorem 5.8], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: Malle's conjecture for 2-groups: linear growth iff there is a transposition. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Shafarevich's theorem (existence of solvable extensions)
items.statement: Every finite solvable group, in particular every 2-group, is a Galois group over every number field.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.2, p.30, citing [Š54], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: IG.4 plans a decomposed proof of Shafarevich's solvable realization theorem.

items.name: Lemma 6.3 and Theorems 6.4–6.5 (thin families without a transposition)
items.statement: The number of degree-2^m 2-extensions K/k with Disc(K/k) = D is O_{[k:ℚ],m,ε}(D^εDisc(k)^{α_m}) (Lemma 6.3). If G ⊆ S_{2^m} is a transitive 2-group without a transposition, disc(K/k) is powerful, so |E_k(G, X)| = O(X^{1/2+ε}Disc(k)^α) (Theorem 6.4), and Σ_{K∈E_k(G,X)}h₃(K/k) = O(X^{1−δ}Disc(k)^α) for some δ > 0 (Theorem 6.5, via Theorem 5.1 and Lemmas 2.1, 4.3, 4.4 with θ = 1/24).
items.locator: Lemma 6.3, Theorems 6.4–6.5 and proofs, pp.31–33, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: Theorem 6.5 improves on the trivial bound X^{1+ε}; the ℓ-torsion conjecture would give X^{1/2+ε}. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Lemmas 6.6–6.9 (wreath-product bookkeeping)
items.statement: A transitive 2-group G ⊂ S_{2d} contains a transposition iff G ≃ C₂ ≀ H for some H ⊂ S_d, with H unique; then a G-extension K/k has a unique subfield F with [K : F] = 2, and F/k is an H-extension (Lemma 6.6). An H-extension F and a quadratic K/F give either a Galois group without a transposition or a G-extension with 2^d compatible identifications, and every G-extension arises once this way (Lemma 6.8). The group signature of K/k is determined by F and that of K/F; |M_F| is independent of F, and Σ_{Σ̄=Σ₀}M_Σ = 2^{r₁(F)}, Σ_{Σ̄=Σ₀}M_Σ3^{−u(Σ)} = 2^{2r₁(F)}/3^{r₁(F)+r₂(F)} (6.7) (Lemma 6.9). Also |Aut_perm(H)|/|Aut_perm(C₂ ≀ H)| = 2^{−2^{m−1}}.
items.locator: Lemmas 6.6–6.9 and proofs, pp.33–35; proof of Theorem 6.1, p.37, citing [Klü12, Lemma 5.5], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: (6.7) was checked. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 6.10 (Datskovsky–Wright)
items.statement: For a number field F and a group signature Σ of quadratic extensions with u(Σ) the relative unit rank: Σ_{[K:F]=2, signature Σ, Disc(K/F)≤X}h₃(K/F) ∼ X·Res_{s=1}ζ_F/(2^{r₁(F)+r₂(F)}ζ_F(2))·(1 + 3^{−u(Σ)}), and the number of such K is ∼ X·Res_{s=1}ζ_F/(2^{r₁(F)+r₂(F)}ζ_F(2)).
items.locator: Theorem 6.10, p.35, citing [DW88, Theorems 4.2, 5.1], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: Imported: the average 3-torsion over quadratic extensions of a fixed base, the key input summed over F. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 6.1 (average 3-torsion in 2-extensions, with signatures and constants)
items.statement: For each m, lim_{X→∞}|E_k(m, X)|^{−1}Σ_{K∈E_k(m,X)}h₃(K) = C_m with C_m = [Σ_F h₃(F)Res ζ_F/(2^{r₂(F)}ζ_F(2)Disc(F)²)·(1 + 2^{r₁(F)}/3^{r₁(F)+r₂(F)})]·[Σ_F Res ζ_F/(2^{r₂(F)}ζ_F(2)Disc(F)²)]^{−1} over F ∈ E_k(m − 1, ∞). For G = C₂ ≀ H ⊂ S_{2^m} a transitive 2-group with a transposition and Σ occurring, the averages over E^Σ_k(G, X) and E_k(G, X) are C_{G,Σ} = [Σ_{F∈E^Σ̄_k(H,∞)}h₃(F)Res ζ_F/(ζ_F(2)Disc(F)²)·(1 + 3^{−u(Σ)})]/[Σ_{F∈E^Σ̄_k(H,∞)}Res ζ_F/(ζ_F(2)Disc(F)²)] and C_G given by the same formula as C_m with the sums over F ∈ E_k(H, ∞) (including the weights 2^{−r₂(F)}).
items.locator: Theorem 6.1, pp.29–30; proof §6.2, pp.35–37, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19 (misprint E6 in the displayed C_G)
items.note: Statement with the C_G weights as derived in the proof (E6). For k = ℚ and G = D₄ this extraction computed C_{D₄} = 1.4230 (weighted 3-torsion averages 1.0039 over real and 1.0549 over imaginary quadratic F, fields |D| ≤ 30000); the displayed formula gives 1.4167. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 1.1 (the average of |Cl_K[3]| for 2-groups with a transposition)
items.statement: For any m, let G ⊂ S_{2^m} be a transitive permutation 2-group containing a transposition. For any number field k there is an explicit constant c_{k,G,3} (Theorem 6.1) with lim_{X→∞}|E_k(G, X)|^{−1}Σ_{K∈E_k(G,X)}|Cl_K[3]| = c_{k,G,3}. For D₄-quartic fields over ℚ the constant is about 1.42; the theorem applies to three groups of degree 8 and 26 of degree 16.
items.locator: Theorem 1.1, p.2, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: The first new (G, p) for the Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet average since (S₂, 3) and (S₃, 2). Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 1.2 = Theorem 6.11 (relative class group averages)
items.statement: For G ⊂ S_{2^m} a transitive 2-group with a transposition, k a number field and u an integer, if E^u_k(G, ∞) ≠ ∅ then lim_{X→∞}|E^u_k(G, X)|^{−1}Σ_{K∈E^u_k(G,X)}|Cl_{K/F_K}[3]| = 1 + 3^{−u}, where F_K is the index-2 subfield and u = rk O_K^* − rk O_{F_K}^*. This is the Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet prediction (Proposition 7.1).
items.locator: Theorem 1.2, p.3; Theorem 6.11 and proof, pp.37–38, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: The first proven case of the Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet conjecture for a function not of the form |Cl_K[p]|, for infinitely many G. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Wang–Wood: Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet moments ([WW21, Theorems 4.1, 6.2, Proposition 6.6])
items.statement: The Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet heuristics agree with the random-group model of [WW21, Conjecture 3.5], and for a G-representation Z over 𝔽₃ with no trivial component the predicted average of |Sur_G(Cl_{K̃}, Z)| is ∏_{v|∞}|Z^{σ_v}|^{−1}, σ_v a decomposition group (complex conjugation) at v.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 7.1, p.38; §7.2, p.39, citing Wang–Wood [WW21], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: Imported. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 7.1 (the prediction for h₃(K/F))
items.statement: With S_K = (1 × C₂^{d−1}) ⋊ Stab_H(1) and S_F = C₂^d ⋊ Stab_H(1) in G = C₂ ≀ H, and U the sign representation of S_F/S_K over 𝔽₃: h₃(K/F) = |Hom_{S_F}(Cl_{K̃/k}, U)|, V = Ind^G_{S_F}U is irreducible, so h₃(K/F) = 1 + |Sur_G(Cl_{K̃/k}, V)|; since Σ_v dim V^{σ_v} is the relative unit rank u, the Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet prediction for the average of h₃(K/F) is 1 + 3^{−u}, as proved in Theorem 6.11.
items.locator: Proposition 7.1 and proof, pp.38–39, citing [CM90, Hypothèse 6.6], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: §7.2: the prediction for h₃(K/k) and the D₄ comparison (Example 7.2)
items.statement: Ind^G_{S_K}𝔽₃ = W × V with W = Ind^G_{S_F}𝔽₃ the permutation representation of H; if W′ = W/𝔽₃ is irreducible, the Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet prediction for the average of h₃(K/k) is (1 + 3^{−u(K/F)})(1 + 3^{−u(F/k)}). For G = D₄ over ℚ, the predictions 1.48, 1.78, 2.67, 2.67 for the four signatures differ from the proven averages ≈ 1.12, 1.34, 2.01, 1.41: the proven average is a weighted average of h₃(F) against Res ζ_F/(ζ_F(2)Disc(F)²), biased by small-discriminant F, as in Bartel–Lenstra's counterexample for cyclic quartics.
items.locator: §7.2, Example 7.2 and table, pp.39–40, citing [BL20], [WW21, Theorem 9.2], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: The four proven values were reproduced in this extraction (1.1155, 1.3386, 2.0078, 1.4066). Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 8.1 (averages for C₂ ≀ H, H arbitrary)
items.statement: For transitive H ⊆ S_n and G = C₂ ≀ H, G-extensions have a unique index-2 subfield F_K, an H-extension. (1) If E^u_k(G, ∞) ≠ ∅ and |E_k(H, X)| ≪ X^{2/3+ε}, then the average of h₃(K/F_K) over E^u_k(G, X) is 1 + 3^{−u}. (2) If E_k(H, ∞) ≠ ∅ and Σ_{F∈E_k(H,X)}h₃(F/k) ≪ X^{2/3+ε}, then the average of h₃(K) over E_k(G, X) tends to an explicit c_{k,G,3}. The hypotheses hold for H ≠ C₂ regular representations realised over k, for nilpotent H without a transposition, and for p-groups with p ≠ 5 odd. Proof: Corollary 3.2 with [BST+20, Theorem 1.1] replaces Theorem 5.1, and [BSW15, Theorem 2] with local conditions at split primes shows that K/k with smaller Galois group contribute o(X).
items.locator: Theorem 8.1 and proof, pp.40–41, citing [BST+20], [BSW15], [EV06], [Alb20], [KM04], [KW20], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e19
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.
